t: Under Hammurabi, a small Amorite city-state became the master of Mesopotamia in barely a decade of conquest.
His Code of 282 laws is the most complete legal collection to survive from the ancient Near East.
Lacking strong institutions, the empire fragmented soon after his death and ended with a Hittite raid around 1595 BCE.
dyk: Hammurabi destroyed the city of Eshnunna not by storming it but by damming and then releasing floodwater against it.
ev: Sumu-abum takes control of Babylon and begins building its walls
Hammurabi defeats an Elamite-led coalition, launching his conquests
Hammurabi conquers Larsa, bringing all southern Mesopotamia under his rule
Hammurabi conquers his former ally Mari
The Code of Hammurabi is inscribed
Hammurabi dies; his son Samsu-iluna soon faces widespread revolt
Hittite king Mursili I sacks Babylon, ending the First Dynasty
